title: Bi-Continuous W-Rich Refractory High Entropy Alloy-Cu Composite: Toward Material Innovation of Nuclear Reactor Coolant System.

recollection.starting_material: Guess: a blend of Cu and a W-rich refractory high-entropy alloy powder (perhaps W-Ta-Mo-Nb-V or similar)
recollection.intervention: Guess: liquid metal dealloying or co-sintering/annealing to produce a bi-continuous phase separation between the HEA and Cu
recollection.structure: Guess: an interpenetrating, bicontinuous network in which the W-rich HEA forms a refractory skeleton while Cu fills the complementary channels
recollection.mechanism: Guess: immiscible phase separation driven by thermodynamic incompatibility between Cu and the multicomponent HEA, leading to spinodal decomposition during solidification/annealing
recollection.results: Guess: high thermal conductivity (>200 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹) from the Cu network combined with high radiation resistance and strength (>1 GPa yield strength at room temperature, retaining >500 MPa at 800 °C) from the HEA, with good corrosion resistance in liquid metal coolants

score.note: The recollection tentatively identifies liquid-metal dealloying but dilutes it with incorrect alternatives and omits the 1200 °C/96 h treatment. The bicontinuous RHEA skeleton/Cu-channel description is broadly correct but largely follows from the title and lacks the aligned morphology and W-rich interlayer. The proposed spinodal/immiscible phase-separation mechanism is wrong; the actual mechanism is selective Ti extraction and Cu replacement with formation of a passivating W-rich interlayer. The thermal-conductivity estimate is substantially too high, and the strength values are unsupported; it also misses the reported conductivity and irradiation-swelling values.
